VBO:0200087.summary: Affectionate and outgoing, Australian Bulldogs can have a stubborn streak. Australian breeders developed the type in the 1990s around companionship, aiming to retain the familiar loyalty and character of a bulldog. Its club maintains an ancestry register to track the population’s continuing development.
VBO:0200087.shortDescription: An affectionate Australian companion type with a stubborn streak, developed to retain a bulldog’s familiar character.

sources.title: Aussie Bulldog Club Australia — breed history
sources.evidence: First-party club history describes affectionate/outgoing character with stubborn tendencies, companion-focused breeding intentions, Queensland programs and1997 inception. These are club/breeder character descriptions and breeding aims, not empirical predictability, health guarantees or recognition.

sources.title: Aussie Bulldog Club Australia — club and ancestry database
sources.evidence: Actual maintaining club home states formationOctober2007 and managed ancestry database of breeders/dogs/lines, supporting maintained current population and continuing development; recognition is an aspiration, not established.

sources.title: Aussie Bulldog Club Australia — Code of Ethics
sources.evidence: Actual club breeding standards limit the program to Aussie/Australian and British Bulldogs and explicitly exclude Southern Cross Bulldogs and Australasian Bosdogs; this is exact scope evidence, not proof of pedigree or health outcomes.

VBO:0201226.summary: The Shiloh Shepherd tends to be sociable and closely attached to its people, often settling calmly after activity. Its association describes dogs taking part in rally, tracking and dock diving, with energy and working drives varying between individuals. Tina Barber began developing the population in the 1970s.
VBO:0201226.shortDescription: A sociable, people-focused companion shepherd, often calm after activity, with varied working drives.

sources.title: International Shiloh Shepherd Alliance — Breed Standard v4.0, April2025
sources.evidence: Entire current five-page standard read in browser and exact extracted PDF text: companion purpose, human focus/eager to please, confident approachable character with friendly/outgoing or aloof/self-possessed alternatives. Some lines retain scent/search/herding ability, not generalized to all dogs. Literal adult head, small-to-medium high erect triangular ears, 9:10 height:length level balanced frame, four limbs/oval feet, plush/smooth coats, and full low plume tail to one bone past hock support morphology. November2022 revision removed therapy/service prospects and wolfish head wording. Child/pet safety, health, guaranteed protection/aptitudes and service claims excluded.

sources.title: International Shiloh Shepherd Alliance — Breed Overview
sources.evidence: Entire current body personally read. Social human focus/attachment, calmer settling/off switch after activity and variation in energy/working drive directly stated. Association reports rally, tracking and dock-diving participation. Founder Tina Barber began work in1970s, own rare-breed separation/ARBA recognition1991; registry goals can differ. No child safety, hip-health improvement, therapy/service guarantees, exact exercise prescription, intelligence ranking or puppy suitability prediction used.

VBO:0200659.summary: Lively, watchful and eager to learn, Harlequin Pinschers tend to form close attachments to their people. Many like to accompany their owners from place to place, and mature dogs are described as composed. The modern American type developed through a 1990 revival of patterned coats using small terrier crosses and Miniature Pinschers.
VBO:0200659.shortDescription: A lively, watchful companion that tends to stay close to its people; a modern American patterned Pinscher type.

sources.title: Continental Kennel Club — Harlequin Pinscher standard and breed history
sources.evidence: Maintaining CKC literal standard describes lively/watchful/eager-to-learn, close people attachment, accompanying owners and mature self-composure. Current named-type history describes modernAmerican1990 merle outcross/breed-back program. Normative breed/program account only, not empirical predictions or oldGerman continuity.
